text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Two Britons intend to buy troubled Banca Dacia Felix SA. They submitted bid to bank's management.
TINERETUL LIBER
- U.S. company Amoco plans to open two petrol stations in northeastern town of Suceava.
- Government approved decree on guaranteed foreign credits for housing construction.
LIBERTATEA
- Government agreed on 6.0 percent wage indexation for state employees in last quarter of 1996.
- State Ownership Fund privatised 2,450 companies so far, of which 78 big ones.
JURNALUL NATIONAL
- Canada's Sarah Cafe International opened modern coffee roasting plant in Romania.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Forty people died in the country's worst viral meningitis epidemic.
- Firefighters put out minor fire aboard Greek oil tanker Palm while on repairs in the Black Sea Mangalia port.
- Some 250 households and 3,500 hectars of farmland were affectd by recent floods in eight counties.
- Social-Democratic Party (PSDR) leader Sergiu Cunescu filed a contest with the Constitutional Court against president Ion Iliescu's running for a third term in November 3 polls.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
ADEVARUL
- The Romanian National Unity Party (PUNR) will not back President Ion Iliescu in second round of presidential polls, PUNR leader Gheorghe Funar said.
- Senate confirmed previous vote on criminal code article providing jail terms for homosexual relations only when they cause "public scandal".
- Lower Chamber of Deputies adopted bill to reverse post-communist law which transferred state assets belonging to former communist youth organisations into NGOs property.
- Former tennis star Ilie Nastase to run for Chamber of Deputies in Harghita county mainly inhabited by Romania's Hungarian minority.
VREMEA
- Socialist Labour Party wants privatisation to be adjourned until after November polls, saying the process in ripping off assets.
AZI
- Ukraine admits increased radiation levels at nuclear plant of Chernobyl.
- Senate criminal code article providing up to five-year jail terms for slender.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Romanian Intelligence Service to come up with proposals to fight corruption.
LIBERTATEA
- Opposition National Peasant Party MPs wanted homosexual relations to be punished.
- Romania signed treaty to ban nuclear tests. ($= 3,246 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
